- When sentiment is consistently negative over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid underestimating rebound.
- After a sharp price spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct — reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and add a slight downward slope to prevent overhang.
- If sentiment flips from negative to positive mid-horizon, model lags in recognizing momentum — increase forecast slope or add early upward bias.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon when price volatility is high — if forecast is far from recent 10-day average, pull toward it with smoothing factor.
- When sentiment is positive and price is trending up, model often underestimates continuation — add 2–3% buffer to forecast tail end.
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to average out — avoid flat forecasts; introduce slight volatility or trend bias based on recent momentum.
